teaser.en: In Diani, the most common Digo way to keep mosquitoes off is to burn the leaves of this fragrant bush.

summary.en: *Chivumbani* is tree basil, an aromatic shrubby herb of bushland and fallow. Its leaves are burned to drive away mosquitoes and used in medicine and spiritual healing.

about.en: *Chivumbani* is an aromatic, shrubby herb with soft, hairy leaves and the square stems of the mint family. Crushed leaves give off a strong, pleasant smell. Small pale flowers grow in spikes at the tips of the stems.

where.en: It grows in bushland and on fallow land.

uses.en:
The leaves are burned to repel mosquitoes. Among the Digo of Diani this is the most common way of keeping them off, reported by more than half of the people asked in one survey.

The leaves are also boiled as a remedy for malaria, inhaled for colds, and used in spiritual healing.

names.en: The Digo name is *chivumbani*. Swahili calls it *kivumbani*. In English it is tree basil.

reason.en: Same genus; African basil, also used in spiritual healing
Another aromatic member of the mint family
Another plant used against malaria and insects
